key_terms: A standalone Metastore service that clients reach over Thrift, separate from the database that persists its records.
The RPC framework and protocol that Hive Metastore clients use. Shared protocol names do not guarantee compatibility across arbitrary releases.
The relational database, here PostgreSQL, that persists Metastore records. Restarting the Thrift service keeps tables only because this database survives.
Creating the Metastore's tables in an empty database with schematool, an explicit action that ordinary startup does not perform.

worked_examples.title: Metadata before and after a stop
worked_examples.code:
cd work/hive
bash run.sh metadata
bash run.sh stop
bash run.sh resume
bash run.sh metadata
bash run.sh check
worked_examples.interpretation: The two metadata reports should match, since the table and partition rows live in PostgreSQL, not in the metastore process. The metastore service itself is stateless; restarting it only proves it can reconnect to the database. The final check then confirms that the data files still answer through HiveServer2. Never run initialize during this test, because it would recreate missing definitions and make a real loss look like success.

worked_examples.title: The metastore database connection
worked_examples.interpretation: This excerpt of conf/hive-site.xml shows the two places that must survive separately: the PostgreSQL metastore database and the warehouse directory. Backing up only one is a common mistake. Restoring the database without the files leaves tables that point at empty locations, and restoring files without the database leaves Parquet that no query can find. Use a consistent pg_dump with the matching file copy and record both identities together.

worked_examples.title: Replacement with a fresh metadata client
worked_examples.code:
cd work/hive
bash run.sh down
bash run.sh start
bash run.sh metadata
bash run.sh check
worked_examples.interpretation: Down removes the containers but keeps the named volumes for PostgreSQL and the warehouse, so start brings up new processes over old state. The metadata probe then reads the table through a brand new Thrift client, which rules out a cached answer from the previous session. If metadata succeeds but check fails, the definitions survived while the warehouse volume did not; if both fail, inspect logs for a database connection or schema version error before trying anything else.

evidence: Prepared actual Hive4.2.1/JDK21/PostgreSQL project; live SQL, independent Java Thrift, lifecycle, Iceberg and restore observations remain distinct acceptance gates.
